Action/Resource may be string or array; normalize to arrays

stories.title: Evaluator: Allow/Deny/NotAction/NotResource semantics

Explicit Deny precedence over Allow within supplied context

stories.title: Risk-rule catalog: wildcard, destructive, exfil, direct-IAM admin

Flag direct IAM administration (iam:*, iam:PutUserPolicy, iam:AttachRolePolicy, iam:CreatePolicyVersion)

stories.title: Phase 2: input caps (DoS) - reject oversized policies instead of hanging
requirements: validate(): enforce a max statement count (e.g. 1000) and reject with a clear error code (TOO_MANY_STATEMENTS) rather than processing
graph builder: enforce a max node/edge count; when exceeded, return a bounded graph plus a visible 'graph truncated' note (findings table stays authoritative)
A 20000-statement policy must resolve (reject or bounded) in-browser well under 5s, never hang the tab
Limits are documented constants; error messages are user-clear
acceptance: a >max-statements fixture yields validate() error, analyze() ok:false, no hang

stories.title: Phase 2: wording precision fixes (correctness of security claims)
requirements: ASSUME-ROLE-EXPANSION: replace 'many roles in the account' with cross-account-accurate wording ('roles across arbitrary AWS accounts whose trust policies permit this principal'); arn:aws:iam::*:role/* spans all accounts

PassRole family: replace 'not restricted with iam:PassedToService, so it can pass a role to this service' with 'does not use iam:PassedToService to restrict which supported AWS services may receive the role' (AWS still enforces service support)
PassRole+EC2/service: replace definitive 'gaining the role permissions' with 'potentially obtaining execution under the passed role credentials' (instance-profile/service behavior still matters)

KMS: separate kms:Decrypt into a distinct Decryption capability finding; do NOT call it 'reads secret material' and do NOT lump it with Secrets Manager. kms:Decrypt decrypts ciphertext for usable keys; it does not enumerate/retrieve secrets
Wildcard rule: drop the 'non-read action' classification; use neutral 'Resource * leaves this action broadly resource-scoped'
acceptance: IAM-semantics critic 100 (every claim technically accurate vs AWS docs)

stories.title: Phase 2: severity remodel (reserve critical for compound escalation)
requirements: critical ONLY for compound escalation paths that plausibly cross a privilege boundary: PassRole+lambda:CreateFunction, PassRole+ec2:RunInstances (and peers), and AssumeRole whose resource scope is effectively all roles (*:role/* or role/*)
Standalone wildcard scope, broad kms:Decrypt, secrets access, direct-IAM single actions remain high
Deterministic, documented severity rules; update every fixture's expected severity to match
acceptance: compound-path fixtures now critical; standalone stay high
no severity is asserted higher than the evidence supports

stories.title: Phase 2: split confidence into policy-evidence vs path-exploitability
requirements: Each finding carries policyEvidence (high|medium|low) AND pathExploitability (high|medium|low), replacing the single confidence field
Example: PassRole+CreateFunction -> policyEvidence high (both perms present), pathExploitability medium (privileged passable role + other controls unknown)
Findings table + evidence panel render both; JSON/MD export includes both
Keep the capability-not-effective limit text on every finding
acceptance: both fields present on all findings
compound paths show evidence>=exploitability where appropriate

stories.title: Phase 2: compound-finding correlation + risk-factor checklist (dedup noise)
requirements: When a standalone wildcard/broad-resource finding is subordinate to a compound escalation path (e.g. PassAnyRole wildcard + LambdaManagement wildcard subsumed by a PassRole->Lambda path), attach it as a risk-factor sub-property of the primary finding, not a separate top-level row
Primary compound finding exposes a risk-factor checklist (present/absent), e.g. [x] iam:PassRole [x] lambda:CreateFunction [x] PassRole Resource:* [ ] iam:PassedToService restriction
Retain standalone wildcard findings ONLY where they do not participate in a compound path
Deterministic subsumption; never drop a genuinely independent finding
acceptance: pass-role compound fixture: one primary path finding with risk factors, no duplicate subordinate wildcard rows
independent wildcard (no compound path) still stands alone

stories.title: Phase 2: risk-summary header above the findings table
requirements: Render a summary block above the table: counts of privilege-escalation paths, role-assumption capabilities, sensitive-data access capabilities, broad-resource grants
Show the single highest-risk path in one line (e.g. Principal -> PassRole -> Lambda -> Passed Role)
Built with safe DOM (createElement+textContent); no inline style/script; accessible
Deterministic ordering and counts
acceptance: summary counts match the findings for fixtures

Row height must drop substantially (current rows are ~650px because 3 prose columns wrap); table stays the authoritative view and remains fully usable/accessible without the graph
Safe DOM only; csp_audit clean; keyboard operable; no prose lost (all still reachable in the detail)
acceptance: avg finding row height well under 120px for a typical multi-finding policy
all prose still present in the expandable detail
full node --test suite green (e2e updated for the new layout)

stories.title: Phase 2: graph encodes the privilege transition (unknown-privileges node)
requirements: For escalation paths, the graph must show the privilege transition, not only the service sequence: Principal -> (iam:PassRole) -> 'Passable Role [unknown privileges]' -> (service action) -> service execution -> 'potential privilege-boundary crossing'
The unknown-privileges node visually distinguishes what the analyzer KNOWS (the grants) from what it does NOT (the target role's actual permissions)
Edges keep evidence + certainty class; SVG text via textContent, numeric attrs only; no markup from input
Deterministic; findings table remains the authoritative equivalent
acceptance: pass-role fixtures render the unknown-privileges transition node

stories.title: Phase 2.1: extend subsumption to same-statement capability findings + summary metric + grammar
requirements: Generalize correlate.js: a generic WILDCARD-RESOURCE finding on a statement that ALSO has a more-specific capability finding for the SAME statement (KMS-DECRYPT, DATA-EXFIL, DIRECT-IAM-ADMIN, DESTRUCTIVE-ACTION, DETECTION-IMPAIRMENT) is subsumed into that capability finding as a risk factor, not a separate top-level row (nothing lost; preserved in subsumed[] + risk factors). Do NOT subsume a WILDCARD-RESOURCE that stands alone (no more-specific finding on that statement) or a full-* WILDCARD-ACTION.

KMS example: kms:Decrypt on * yields ONE primary KMS-DECRYPT finding with risk factors [x] kms:Decrypt granted [x] Resource:* [ ] kms:ViaService restriction [ ] kms:EncryptionContext restriction; total primaries drop from 6 to 5
Rename the risk-summary metric 'Broad-resource grants' to 'Standalone broad-resource findings' (count reflects post-subsumption standalone wildcards only)
Fix grammar in rules.js: 'Grants actions that reads secret material' -> 'read secret material'
acceptance: KMS fixture: 5 primaries, no duplicate WILDCARD-RESOURCE row for the KMS statement
a genuinely standalone wildcard-resource still stands alone

stories.title: Phase 2.1: graph edge certainty vocabulary + can-decrypt edge type
requirements: PassRole->service transition edges: change certainty from 'confirmed-by-context' to 'policy-supported' (the policy confirms the grants but NOT that a usable target role / trust config exists). Keep AssumeRole as 'potentially-reachable'. Certainty vocabulary: confirmed-by-policy (a grant literally in the policy), policy-supported (grants present but transition needs an out-of-scope precondition), potentially-reachable, context-required, blocked-by-deny, unknown-incomplete-context.

Introduce a distinct graph edge type 'can-decrypt' for kms:Decrypt (was 'can-read'); keep the human label 'can decrypt ciphertext'. Update the edge-type ontology and render-graph legend/styles so can-decrypt is visually distinct from can-read.
Update graph fixtures + tests for the new certainty values and edge type; keep SVG text via textContent, injection fixtures inert
acceptance: pass-role transition edges are policy-supported (not confirmed-by-context)

stories.title: Phase 3: author + validate the negative regression corpus (does-not-fire truth)
requirements: Create fixtures under fixtures/negative/ - each a policy + expected outcome (findingIds it MUST produce, notFindingIds/severities it MUST NOT overstate) + a `rationale` field citing the AWS behavior that makes the expectation correct. These assert the engine knows when NOT to fire (or to lower severity).

Cover at least these cases: (1) same dangerous actions split across two statements -> compound STILL detected across statements; (2) iam:PassRole restricted by iam:PassedToService pinned to a service that does NOT match the exec action -> that escalation path NOT flagged; (3) iam:PassRole scoped to one specific harmless role ARN -> not flagged as broad; (4) explicit Deny conflicting with Allow on the same action -> deny suppresses; (5) NotAction semantics; (6) NotResource semantics; (7) Condition StringEquals/StringLike narrowing -> acknowledged / lower confidence; (8) permissions-boundary-shaped policy; (9) resource-based / trust policy -> NO identity-escalation finding; (10) read-only-admin wildcard (e.g. Get*/Describe*/List* on *) -> broad but NOT privileged-escalation/critical; (11) action where AWS REQUIRES Resource:* (e.g. ec2:DescribeInstances) -> not penalized as an avoidable wildcard; (12) cross-account AssumeRole constrained to ONE account id (arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/*) -> lower than all-accounts *:role/*; (13) lambda:UpdateFunctionCode WITHOUT iam:PassRole -> not a PassRole escalation; (14) iam:PassRole WITHOUT any workload-execution primitive -> not escalation; (15) two escalation chains sharing one PassRole primitive.

This story authors DATA + rationale ONLY. Do NOT modify engine code. Do NOT wire the corpus into the blocking test suite yet (the engine may not satisfy all cases - that is IAM-302's job). Keep the existing suite green (fixtures added are inert until wired).
acceptance: fixtures/negative/ has >=15 fixtures, each with policy + expect + rationale
IAM-semantics critic 100: EVERY expected outcome is correct per real AWS semantics (an incorrect expectation is blocking - this is the integrity gate)
existing full node --test suite still green

stories.title: Phase 3: wire the negative corpus + fix the engine to match the validated truth
requirements: Add tests/negative.test.js that runs every fixtures/negative/ fixture through analyze() and asserts engine output matches the fixture's expected outcome (findingIds present, notFindingIds absent, severities not overstated).

For each failing case, FIX THE ENGINE (rules.js / escalation.js / correlate.js) so it produces the correct result. The negative fixtures + their rationale are FROZEN TRUTH from IAM-301: do NOT weaken or edit an expectation to make a test pass. If a fixture expectation is genuinely wrong, STOP and flag it (do not silently bend it).

Likely engine fixes: cross-statement compound detection; honor iam:PassedToService service-match before flagging a PassRole path; do not flag PassRole scoped to a specific role or PassRole-without-exec; explicit-Deny suppression; NotAction/NotResource; single-account vs all-accounts AssumeRole severity; treat AWS-required Resource:* actions as not-an-avoidable-wildcard where determinable; read-only wildcards not escalation.
Preserve all Phase-1/2/2.1 behavior; keep determinism, safe DOM, zero egress.
acceptance: tests/negative.test.js green: engine matches every validated negative fixture
no negative-fixture expectation was weakened (diff shows engine changes, not expectation changes)
IAM-semantics critic 100 (no false allow/deny, no overstated severity)

stories.title: Phase 4: path-focused, lane-grouped attack-path graph
requirements: Group graph paths into labeled semantic lanes instead of a flat radial layout where every node competes: PRIVILEGE ESCALATION (PassRole -> Passable Role [unknown privileges] -> service execution -> potential boundary crossing), IDENTITY EXPANSION (AssumeRole -> role scope), DATA ACCESS (secrets retrieval, KMS decryption, bulk object read - each its own path from Principal), SCOPE (standalone broad-resource / Resource:*).

The graph model (graph.js) assigns each edge/path to a lane; render-graph.js draws labeled lane sections (a heading per non-empty lane) with the paths inside, so escalation paths read top-to-bottom and don't visually compete with data-access or scope nodes.

Preserve everything from earlier phases: the 'Passable Role [unknown privileges]' transition node, certainty styles (policy-supported/potentially-reachable/etc.), can-decrypt vs can-read edge types, per-edge evidence on select, reduced-motion, and SVG text via textContent (injection-inert).

The findings table remains the authoritative view; the graph is still a progressive-enhancement aid and must stay keyboard-accessible with an equivalent accessible representation. Empty lanes are omitted (no empty headings).
Deterministic layout/ordering; enforce the existing max-node cap.
acceptance: a multi-category policy renders distinct PRIVILEGE ESCALATION / IDENTITY EXPANSION / DATA ACCESS / SCOPE lane sections
escalation paths show the unknown-privileges transition node within their lane
graph injection fixtures still inert; reduced-motion honored
full node --test suite green (graph fixtures/e2e updated)
